source.title: Do Transformers Grok Succinct Algorithms? Mechanistic Evidence for Counting Circuits

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the original IOI study but does not test IOI or rely on its circuit. Its own experiments concern binary counting and addition, not indirect object identification.
record.gate_note: No IOI prompts, GPT-2 small IOI interventions, or measurements of the IOI circuit are reported. Rows below record related but different counting/addition findings only; they do not test any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Wang et al. (2023) only as a source for activation patching. Its experiments cover binary counting in a 2-layer RoPE Transformer and space-delimited addition in Pythia-160M. It reports no IOI prompts, no GPT-2 small, and no measurement of name-mover, S-inhibition or duplicate-token heads, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct but incomplete. The authors conclude that gradient-trained Transformers, unlike RNNs and SSMs, learn succinct counting circuits through a grokking 'complexity collapse' under weight decay. The learned circuit uses RoPE same-bit lookup heads and XOR/AND MLPs. Pythia-160M shows suggestive analogous routing heads, pending quantitative verification.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes counting and addition rather than IOI, and uses a different task and circuit specification; its activation-patching procedure is a general interpretability technique, not a reproduction of the original IOI analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: For the counting task, generalization depends on weight decay: low regularization leaves memorization, λ=1.0 induces grokking, and λ=2.0 underfits. Stratified sampling extends success to rare carry chains. Pythia's routing pattern is reported as contingent on space-delimited digit tokenization.

fits_no_version.finding: In a grokked 2-layer RoPE Transformer on binary counting, activation patching gives the largest logit-difference drops for L0H2 (0.85–0.90) and the L0 MLP (0.92–0.98). The authors read these as a retrieval head and a logic MLP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small Transformers trained on binary counting implement same-bit lookup in attention and carry logic in MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia-160M on space-delimited addition, a few heads (e.g. L8H5) have diagonal attention scores above 0.9, while over 95% of heads score below 0.2. The authors call this qualitative only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained LMs contain sparse digit-aligned routing heads for addition when digits are tokenised separately.

fits_no_version.finding: The counting model trained at n=20 fails at positions p≥20 when evaluated at n=25.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The learned counting circuit does not extrapolate to relative offsets outside the training range.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code and trained checkpoints will be released upon publication, but gives no URL)
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics; Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics, ACL 2026
record.problems: The paper's Pythia evidence is described as exploratory and qualitative, and the authors say quantitative verification remains pending. The synthetic Transformer depends on stratified sampling and specific regularization; the paper also reports failure to generalize to longer sequences beyond its training horizon. Patch-table values are reported without uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: All of it: the GPT-2 small IOI circuit, its 26 heads in 7 classes, and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
Backup name-mover heads and self-repair under ablation.
IOI circuits in other models, sizes or checkpoints, and reuse of IOI components. The counting and addition circuits are different tasks with different head roles.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics recover the IOI circuit.
Sensitivity of IOI circuit evaluation to ablation, metric and prompt distribution.
IOI across name orders, templates and numbers of names.

record.verdict_notes: Not relevant to IOI. The only connection is the citation of Wang et al. for the activation patching method. The record's relation and tranche (cites_only, T6) are correct.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small IOI circuit, its 26 heads and 7 classes, and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Backup heads taking over the IOI name-mover role after ablation.
IOI circuits in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, and reuse of the IOI components for other tasks. The paper reports only qualitative analogies in different tasks.
Whether alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover the IOI circuit.
IOI circuit evaluation under different ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions.
IOI across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.
